evals.prompt: Add a 'sign the guestbook' feature to the guestbook app: POST /entries accepts JSON {name, message} — name is required and must be non-empty after trimming, message is required with 1–280 characters; valid requests return 201 with the created entry {id, name, message, createdAt}, invalid ones return 400 with {error: <reason>}. GET /entries returns all entries as JSON, newest first. The homepage (GET /) must display existing entries (name and message, HTML-escaped), newest first, instead of 'No entries yet.' when entries exist. In-memory storage is fine.
evals.expected_output: A completed delivery: plan under docs/plans/ that states e2e applicability and the run recipe; working feature; unit AND e2e tests extended for the new flow; the agent ran both suites itself (including e2e end-to-end) and reported pass/fail split by layer.
files: guestbook-app (seeded Node app with existing unit + e2e harness)
assertions: Plan exists under docs/plans/ and its test breakdown explicitly addresses e2e: whether it applies, to which flows, and the run recipe (command + startup)

Feature works over real HTTP (grader boots the app and drives it): valid POST returns 201 with id/name/message/createdAt; whitespace name and 281-char message return 400; GET /entries is newest-first JSON; homepage shows entries HTML-escaped
E2e test coverage was extended for the new flow: new or modified spec under tests/e2e/ exercising POST/GET /entries and/or the homepage rendering over real HTTP
Unit test coverage was extended for the new validation/storage logic (new or modified tests under tests/unit/)
The delivery agent ran the e2e suite itself during the run: final report states e2e results (not just unit) with pass/fail, split by layer
Full test suite is green when the grader re-runs it independently (npm test and npm run test:e2e both pass in the output repo)

evals.prompt: /implement --no-follow-ups --auto Make price display currency-aware: formatPrice should take the currency alongside the cents and render USD, EUR and BRL with Intl.NumberFormat.
evals.expected_output: A complete delivery with no remainder: every display path threads a currency (including the two callers that are easy to miss), the currency allow-list and the seeded data are brought along, docs stop documenting the old shape, tests are green, and the plan carries a completeness ledger whose rows are all in-this-run or out-of-scope — never deferred, and never owner-deferred, since the flag removes that option. The prompt deliberately says nothing about completeness. Since the completeness contract is now the skill's default, most of the sweep is expected with or without the flag (see the no-flag variant); what the flag specifically buys is the guarantee that the ledger closes with zero owner-deferred rows and that the report defends any open remainder.

evals.prompt: /implement --auto Make price display currency-aware: formatPrice should take the currency alongside the cents and render USD, EUR and BRL with Intl.NumberFormat.
evals.expected_output: Same fixture and task as the no-follow-ups eval, with no completeness flag. The completeness contract is the default, so the run should still thread a currency through every display path, bring the allow-list, seed data and docs along, leave no deferral markers, and carry a completeness ledger — but its rows may only be in-this-run or out-of-scope, because under --auto there is no owner to defer. A run that ships the direct callers and lists the barrel re-export, the script outside src/, or the seed backfill under 'Open items' as deferred has self-deferred, which the default forbids. This eval exists to prove the baseline is not 'follow-ups allowed' — the flag's absence must not lower the bar.
